scoring: Match findings to scenarios by the bucket name in terraform output scenario_resources. Score each scenario against the highest-severity finding that cites it, or NONE if no finding cites it. A scenario passes when that result is in acceptable_severities and, if cited, the finding's category is expected.category or in acceptable_categories. NONE on a scenario that does not accept NONE is a false negative; a rating above acceptable_severities on an expected or minor scenario is a false positive. When deferral_acceptable is true, PARTIAL or INSUFFICIENT confidence counts as an appropriate deferral.
rating_method: Likelihood follows CCSS (NIST IR 7502) exploitability concepts aligned with Vista's definitions: HIGH when reachable from the Internet and usable without credentials; MEDIUM when one precondition must hold first (a credential or API key, a foothold inside the network, an application flaw, or compromise of the resource); LOW when prior account-level access is needed or the issue is defense in depth only. Impact follows CCSS confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact, widened by the mapped ATT&CK technique's outcome: HIGH for account-wide reach, privilege escalation, or full read/write/delete of data; MEDIUM when confined to the resource or one data store; LOW for minor or visibility-only impact. Severity comes from Vista's likelihood x impact matrix. fsbp_reference_severity is the highest published FSBP severity among controls that fail because of the scenario's change (controls that fail on every resource are listed in baseline_controls and excluded). acceptable_severities is the expected severity plus one adjacent level: toward the FSBP reference when one exists and differs, otherwise toward the axis the rationale marks as uncertain. Expected scenarios accept NONE and LOW; ambiguous scenarios accept one level on each side plus deferral. A context_override means documented context removes the attack path FSBP assumes, so the range moves at most one level toward the reference.
action_method: expected_action is what a person should do about the scenario: REMEDIATE for dangerous and minor, REVIEW for ambiguous, NO_ACTION for expected. It is derived from kind, not rated separately. Severity and action are scored independently.

baseline_controls.note: Fail regardless of scenario; excluded from per-scenario references.

controls.scope: No lifecycle configuration on versioned buckets
No Object Lock (passes on db-backups only)

kinds.dangerous: A real weakness Vista must report within the acceptable range.
kinds.ambiguous: Defensible either way; the model should explain the tradeoff or defer. NONE and over-rating are both wrong.
kinds.expected: A correctly configured resource; NONE or a LOW hygiene note.
kinds.minor: A small, real gap; LOW or no finding.

change_log.reason: The research question asks Vista to separate resources needing remediation from expected configurations and cases needing human review. The review format previously had no way to say the last two, so Vista now emits a Recommended action field and the ground truth records the matching answer.

scenarios.title: CORS allows any origin to send GET, PUT, and DELETE
scenarios.rationale: CORS grants no access on its own; the bucket is private and TLS-only, so this only matters if a caller already has credentials or a presigned URL.

scenarios.title: public-read ACL lets anyone list object names
scenarios.rationale: AllUsers READ on the bucket survives Block Public Access and BucketOwnerPreferred ownership, so anyone can list keys; object contents stay private.

framework_mappings.context_override: The public grant allows listing object names only; object contents stay private.

scenarios.title: Wildcard principal can read and write objects from any account in the organization
scenarios.rationale: aws:PrincipalOrgID keeps it non-public, but any principal in any org account can read and overwrite data, which needs an org foothold first.

framework_mappings.note: S3.6 does not fail: its fixed denylist covers policy- and ACL-changing actions, not GetObject or PutObject.

scenarios.title: Bucket policy allows anonymous s3:GetObject
scenarios.rationale: Principal * with no condition and Block Public Access policy flags off: every object is readable by anyone on the Internet.

scenarios.title: Bucket policy allows anonymous read, write, and delete
scenarios.rationale: Anyone can read, overwrite, and delete objects with no credentials, enabling data theft, tampering, destruction, and malware hosting.

scenarios.title: Static website bucket with anonymous read
scenarios.rationale: Website hosting is enabled and anonymous GetObject is the purpose of the bucket; SSE-S3 and no TLS-only rule are required for S3 website endpoints. Without account intent the model cannot confirm the content is meant to be public, and FSBP rates the public read Critical, so MEDIUM or HIGH with that caveat, or a deferral, is correct. CRITICAL treats a website as a data leak.

framework_mappings.context_override: Static website hosting is enabled and anonymous read is its purpose; S3 website endpoints require HTTP and SSE-S3.

scenarios.title: Anonymous read limited to the public/ prefix
scenarios.rationale: Only objects under public/ are anonymously readable and the rest of the bucket is private. Whether that is a leak depends on what is stored there, which the facts do not show; the model should name the prefix scope and ask for confirmation rather than call the whole bucket public.

framework_mappings.context_override: Only objects under public/ are anonymously readable.

scenarios.title: Anonymous read restricted only by aws:Referer
scenarios.rationale: The Referer header is set by the client, so anyone can send it; the policy is effectively anonymous read of every object, and AWS reports it as public. Tests whether the model treats a spoofable condition as a real restriction.

scenarios.title: Fully hardened application configuration bucket
scenarios.rationale: Block Public Access on, ACLs disabled, SSE-KMS, versioning, access logging, and TLS-only.

scenarios.title: Fully hardened backup bucket with Object Lock
scenarios.rationale: Same as app-config plus Object Lock enabled. A note that no default retention is set is reasonable but no more than LOW.

scenarios.title: Private scratch bucket without versioning or access logging
scenarios.rationale: Private, encrypted, and TLS-only; missing versioning and logging only reduce recoverability and visibility. FSBP rates missing server access logging (S3.9) Medium, so MEDIUM is also accepted.
